## Mission

In adventure 7, you audited a problematic report and prepared a more responsible version of the data. The challenge is to turn that work into a short, clear and reusable note.

Your goal is to convince a reader that your improved visualizations are more honest than the initial version, and that your data protection choices genuinely reduce risk.

## Expected Work

Starting from your `STT-1100/aventure-7` repository, produce a final version of `rapport_ethique.qmd`.

The report must contain:

- a "Problems identified" section with at least five specific issues;
- an "Anonymized data" section describing the columns removed, grouped or transformed;
- a "Responsible visualizations" section with at least two corrected visualizations;
- a "Limitations" section explaining what the data do not allow you to conclude;
- a short personal conclusion from each team member.

## Anonymized File

Your repository must also contain a `covid_module7_anonymise.csv` file.

This file must not contain:

- names;
- emails;
- phone numbers;
- dates of birth;
- precise individual coordinates;
- free-text notes that could identify a person.

If you keep sensitive variables such as age, sex, occupation or certain medical conditions, explain why they are necessary and how you reduce re-identification risk.

## Visualizations

Each visualization must:

- use an honest scale;
- avoid colors that suggest an unjustified judgment;
- display or mention counts;
- have a descriptive title;
- be accompanied by a careful interpretation.

A strong answer does not try to produce the most spectacular charts. It tries to produce charts that can be defended.

## Deliverables

Your GitHub repository must contain:

- `rapport_ethique.qmd`;
- `rapport_ethique.html`;
- `covid_module7_anonymise.csv`;
- `README.md`;
- the starter files if you kept them to document your process.

## Evaluation Grid

| Criterion | Excellent | Satisfactory | Needs improvement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical audit | Problems are precise, varied and supported by observable elements | Problems are relevant, but sometimes general | Problems are vague or incomplete |
| Anonymization | Direct identifiers are removed and residual risks are discussed | Direct identifiers are removed, but the discussion remains limited | Identifying information remains |
| Visualization | The charts are clear, honest, readable and interpreted carefully | The charts are understandable, but some choices remain weakly justified | The charts reproduce biases from the initial version or only one visualization is provided |
| Reproducibility | The report renders without error and the README explains the procedure | The report renders, but the procedure is weakly documented | The report does not render or necessary files are missing |

## Checklist Before Submission

- `rapport_ethique.qmd` renders without error.
- `rapport_ethique.html` is present.
- `covid_module7_anonymise.csv` contains no direct identifiers.
- The report contains at least two corrected visualizations.
- Limitations are explicitly stated.
- Conclusions remain descriptive and careful.
